text:
sales-ash: Heads up — CrestWave (Dedicated) reporting intermittent 401s during traffic spikes. Customer says "requests sometimes return 'missing auth' only under bursts. They want a patch ASAP, flagged as high priority.

anita: Thanks Ash. Any logs or repro? Which pool/region?

sales-ash: Logs here: https://redwood.logs/crestwave/incident/4321 — looks like header gets dropped between LB and runtime when connection churn is high. Region us-west-2, pool cw-ded-1. Started ~2026-03-20T10:12PT. Customer asking for ETA.

sanjay: I can confirm a spike in 401 rate coinciding with connection churn. Repro locally with a small load test. Suspect LB->runtime keepalive handling where second chunk reads lose the Authorization header. Quick fix: ensure header passthrough and adjust accept loop timeout. Patch is a small change in nginx/proxy layer + a runtime accept guard.

lucy: We need to choose hotfix vs next minor. Given this is customer-facing auth failures I lean hotfix. Risk: rolling restart of dedicated nodes -> brief latency blips. Recommend canary first.

anita: Proposed plan: hotfix branch -> deploy to a single canary pool cw-ded-1-canary at 2% traffic for 4 hours. Monitor 401 rate and p95 latency. If stable, promote to remaining pools with 10-min staggers. Rollback = remove traffic to canary + revert config. Minimal downtime for customer.

sanjay: Patch ready in branch fix/ingress-header-passthrough. Build + smoke tests ~30m. I can start the canary deploy at 14:00 UTC. Smoke test includes: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://cw-ded-1-canary/api/health` and a short load replay.

jamie: I'll own the runbook and deployment orchestration. Runbook steps: create canary pool, route 2% traffic, set alerts (401 > baseline + 5/min), manual approval after 4h. Prepare rollback steps and escalation contacts.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: create cw-ded-1-canary -> route 2% traffic -> attach monitors (simulated).

lucy: Comms: sales to notify CrestWave with schedule: canary at 14:00 UTC, expected no downtime, monitoring in place, update within 4h on promotion. Ops to post any incident notes in #incidents. @sales-ash please confirm wording.

sales-ash: Confirmed, I'll send: "We will run a controlled canary at 14:00 UTC; we expect no downtime. We'll monitor and notify within 4 hours about promotion or rollback." They prefer platform fix vs temporary proxy.

anita: Decision: hotfix via canary. Owners: Sanjay (patch + smoke), Jamie (deploy/runbook), Lucy (rollback & comms), Sales-Ash (customer comms). Target: complete by EOD. Revert within 15m if regressions. I'll mark PROD-8123 as hotfix.

jamie: Runbook checklist I'll post shortly. Quick pre-deploy tests: single `curl` with Authorization header, small burst load to validate 401s drop, check trace IDs.

sanjay: On successful canary, I'll roll to other dedicated pools with 10-min gaps. Full rollout ETA ~3h after canary success.

anita: :thumbsup: thanks team. I'll update the intake ticket with timeline and acceptance criteria: 1) 401 rate returns to baseline during 4h canary, 2) no >5% increase in p95 latency, 3) smoke tests pass.

jamie: I'll also add telemetry to the canary dashboard: auth_fail_rate, avg_latency, error_budgets. Posting runbook link once ready.

sales-ash: Noted. I'll keep the customer updated and include rollback triggers.

anita: Closing loop here — hotfix plan approved. Will track on call at 13:50 UTC for final go/no-go.
